subtopic: CUDA / Warp size, warp scheduling, and SIMT execution
learningObjective: Reason about warp granularity: how threads are grouped into warps and how a warp is scheduled as a single instruction issue unit.
stem: Which statement about NVIDIA warp execution is correct?

options.text: A warp is a group of 32 threads (`warpSize == 32`) that the SM schedules as a single instruction issue unit; all 32 lanes execute the same instruction on their respective data (SIMT), with per-lane predication used when a branch would otherwise diverge.

Warp size is architecture-dependent and has ranged from 16 to 128 across NVIDIA generations; portable kernels should query `blockDim.x % warpSize == 0` at runtime and adapt block dimensions accordingly.

Warps are software-only abstractions imposed by nvcc for readability; the underlying hardware schedules individual threads independently, and warp-level primitives (shuffles, votes) are software emulations.
Threads in a warp are scheduled in a round-robin order at instruction granularity; even for non-divergent code, each thread of the warp takes 32 cycles to complete one instruction.

explanation: A warp is 32 threads on all current NVIDIA architectures; the SM's warp scheduler issues one instruction per warp per cycle (per scheduler; modern SMs have multiple schedulers). SIMT means every lane executes the same instruction; when a branch would diverge, lanes are predicated off, resulting in serialization of the divergent paths. The 32-thread size is a fixed hardware property (`warpSize == 32`). Warp-level primitives (`__shfl_*_sync`, `__any_sync`, etc.) map to actual hardware operations. Choice B is fabricated; warp size has been 32 for the entirety of NVIDIA's CUDA lineup.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: warp = 32 threads; SIMT + predication for divergence.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: warpSize has been 32 on all NVIDIA CUDA GPUs.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: warps are a hardware concept; primitives use real HW ops.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: SIMT executes 32 lanes in parallel; not round-robin.

assumptions: NVIDIA CUDA GPUs (as opposed to hypothetical wave-64 architectures like AMD).
nonImplications: Does not imply divergent code is always slow; divergence within a warp is where it hurts.
Does not imply lane scheduling is fully SIMT on Volta+; Independent Thread Scheduling allows lanes to make forward progress independently in specific cases.

distractorRationales.B: Fabricates variable warp size on NVIDIA.
distractorRationales.D: Confuses SIMT parallel issue with serial round-robin.
